evidence: The existing regional ṭhēhunā knee/elbow family is registered in extensions_ia.csv e82 and includes Chitwan ṭhehun knee. Independently, full Platts p.366 gives ṭhewnā/ṭheʼonā/ṭheʼunā knee and nasalized variants. The selected Danuwar/Tharu knee responses are grouped provisionally in this regional family, preserving medial h, vowels, nasalization and final ī/u/a. This is family membership only: it does not establish the starred head as an ancient reconstruction or adopt Platts’s aṣṭhīvan derivation. Earlier elbow-semantic concerns remain separate; these responses mean knee. Regional IA transmission remains unresolved.

Full CDIAL ghuṭa subsection 2 ghuṇṭa explicitly gives Kumaoni ghuno knee, Nepali ghũṛo and Gujarati ghũṭaṇ knee. Dotyali gũṇā̃/ghuṇā/ghũṇā/ghudā and Majhi/Bote ghõḍa/ghõra/ghũḍa/ghora knee fit this nasal regional branch, with source aspiration, nasalization, retroflex stop/rhotic and final-vowel notation preserved and qualified. The separately numbered ghuṭṭa Hindi ghuṭnā branch is not substituted merely on the knee gloss. Regional IA transmission and local phonetic developments remain unresolved.
